facts.fact: Corbeau News Centrafrique reports that national identity cards (CNI) are being issued through police and registry offices in Ndele and other towns including Bangui, with applicants demanding payment of 100,000 to 200,000 CFA francs.
The article says the $13m SNID, built around a unique identification number, has feasibility studies done and an international tender and procurement ahead, with implementation 2027-2032.

slug: 2025-07-27 Centrafrique - le prix des cartes d'identite reduit apres cinq ans de violations de la loi

facts.fact: Corbeau News Centrafrique reports the government cut the national identity card (CNI) price to 4,500 FCFA by interministerial order of 26 June 2025, after citizens paid 6,000-6,750 FCFA for five years under a public-private arrangement with the firm Almadina, and says the card is indispensable to vote.

systems.owner: Government of the Central African Republic, with the firm Almadina as partner

slug: 2025-12-08 RCA - la societe Al-Madina deploie sa mission d'identite a Birao

facts.fact: Journal de Bangui reports that Al-Madina's team is enrolling applicants for the secure national identity card in Birao, capturing biometric data, photos and personal information, after Bouar and Berberati.

slug: 2024-10-08 Central African Republic in full biometric voter registration preparations

facts.fact: Biometric Update reports national ID cards are issued in Central African Republic, but only in the capital because of insecurity, with an enrolment centre opened in Bambari.

note: A police circular lists a biometric national ID card among accepted border documents, but the document does not say the country issues one.
